key_insight: OUCH combines pneumatic actuation with focused indenter geometry to deliver controlled wrist stimulation and elicit discomfort at approximately 89% lower applied force than a handheld pressure algometer.
engineering_relevance: A compact wearable actuator could standardize stimulus delivery for neurological assessment while reducing reliance on variable manual techniques.
method: Stacked pneumatic pouch actuators drive a rigid indenter.
A compliant spacer buckles at a set load, allowing skin contact only during actuation.
Finite element analysis and deformable-testbed measurements characterize tissue loading.
evidence_signal: Blocked-force tests, clinician evaluation, finite element analysis, and preliminary perceptual testing supported an estimated contact pressure of 18,500 kPa at 200 kPa inflation and comparable deformation at depth to the algometer.
watch_item: Preliminary discomfort results do not establish safety or diagnostic validity in patients with disorders of consciousness.
paper_title: OUCH: Objective, Uniform, Controlled Haptic Stimulation for Automated Neurological Assessment
